item.title: Cicero on Our Disengaged Age
item.description: The collapse of the late Roman republic came not in an instant but over time: through a period of profound internal fracture and systemic chaos. As we approach the 250th anniversary of the American founding, we find ourselves in a similar period of civic fragmentation and disengagement.

item.title: America’s Conflict in Iran Is Not a Just War
item.description: Unlike the Iraq war, Trump’s Iran war is being fought without a clear plan or congressional approval. For these and other reasons, it plainly does not meet the conditions for a morally acceptable war, as set out by traditional just war doctrine.

item.title: A Sacramental Theology of Marriage: A Q&amp;A with Fr. José Granados
item.description: This book invites spouses to look beyond themselves to better understand the greatness of the gift they have received and make it fruitful.

item.title: Beautiful Losers
item.description: The job of present-day conservatives isn't to tear down, lament, and criticize. Instead we should attempt to preserve the good, while mending those things that are broken.

item.title: Beware the Cul-De-Sac of Weirdness
item.description: The human future, if there is to be one worth having, will be normal; that is to say, it will conserve the things that have always been good for the human to have, hold, cherish, and sometimes fight for.

item.title: Conservatism’s Formation Crisis
item.description: Conservatism, if it deserves the name, cannot be merely a marketplace of grievances or a contest of personalities. It must be a training ground for judgment ordered to the good of persons, families, communities, and the political order.

item.title: Zohran Mamdani Is Not Radical Enough
item.description: Dorothy Day’s radical call to love rings louder for us today than Zohran’s Servile State solution ever will.

item.title: The Bookshelf: The Return of Sybil
item.description: If the witch crazes of recovered memory and multiple personalities are making a comeback, perhaps now aided by social contagion online, we would do well to gird ourselves with a sound understanding of psychiatry’s vulnerability to misdirection—and of the harm it can do to the souls under its care.

item.title: Günther Anders’s Bleak Picture of the Tech-Perfected Society
item.description: We are using our genius to degrade ourselves into nothing much at all, and the existential results are anxiety and shame at how small we have become.

item.title: When Religion Becomes Obsolete, Politics Tries to Save Us
item.description: When politics becomes our highest love, it will also become our cruelest disappointment, leaving our homes colder, our holidays lonelier, and our common life harder to sustain.

item.title: Language and the Politics of Power
item.description: Increasingly in our society and politics, the value of life has been subordinated to the aims and narratives of manipulative discourse. The Holy Father is right to warn us of this danger.

item.title: The Dark History of American Nativism
item.description: For all its failures and drawbacks—and there are many—American culture’s focus on individual freedom is intoxicating and infectious.

item.title: Edgardo Mortara Should Not Have Been Taken from His Parents
item.description: An in-depth review of Matthew Tapie’s The Mortara Case and Thomas Aquinas’s Defense of Jewish Parental Authority

item.title: On the Killing of Enemy Sovereigns

item.description: The ideal speech situation is not Habermas’s greatest legacy.
